- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
No trials have run yet, and the starting architecture scores 0.000 on both seeds. Getting off zero is the first goal. To place a brick correctly, the agent has to find the brick's landing layer, which is the highest filled cell under its footprint. It then has to check that the target has every cell the brick fills at that layer, and that the brick does not seal off target cells below it. The starting head pools column features over each footprint, but it never looks at the target at the specific layer where the brick would land. That makes the exact per-layer check hard to learn. The budget is also small: the default recipe gives only 32 updates. So this round is a 2x2-style test of a layer-aware placement head and a recipe with more samples and more updates. Candidate A changes only the network, B changes only the recipe, and C combines both.

### Round 2
All four trials scored 0, both on dev and on training success in the last 10% of steps. That held for two heads, each with two recipes (32 to 113 updates). With nothing above zero there is no signal yet, so the job now is to get any learning at all. Possible causes: (1) too few fresh samples or updates, since exact builds need every placement right and the +1 bonus is rare; (2) the hand-aligned footprint pooling assumes the anchor rules as described, but the world may differ (anchor offset, swapped axes), and a misaligned head would never place cleanly; (3) DONE and placement order need global context that pooled CNN features give only weakly. I propose: the baseline with 1 PPO epoch for about 3x more samples plus a longer horizon; a residual CNN whose output conv learns its own alignment and sees global context; and a small transformer over cells for global reasoning.

### Round 3
All 6 trials scored exactly 0 on dev, and training success was also 0 in every trial. The trials covered footprint-pooled heads, a layer-aware head, a learned 3x3 output conv, a transformer, and recipes giving up to 3x the samples with 1–2 PPO epochs. A simple per-column 1x1 policy should solve some small designs, so a perception gap or too few samples cannot easily explain all-zero results across such different networks. A more likely cause is the world note: the action layout, footprint order or DONE index may differ from the description. Every head so far ties logits to cells by a fixed spatial alignment, which would break if the action layout is different. This round tests heads that learn the action-to-cell mapping themselves: a full linear action head, a pure MLP, and learned action queries that attend over cells. Each head also feeds the legality mask in as input, because the mask shows the real layout of the action space.

### Round 4
After 9 trials every result is 0.000. Training success is also 0, so this is not a problem with dev generalisation. The 9 trials covered very different networks: footprint pooling, layer-aware heads, a learned 3x3 output conv, a full linear head, a plain MLP, attention and action queries. They also covered recipes with 1 to 4 epochs and 94k to 408k samples. With no gradient between them, the evidence can't rank any idea, and 2-seed noise adds nothing here. The most likely cause is that training never samples an exact build, so the +1 bonus is never seen. Shaped reward alone may push the policy towards sloppy big bricks, or towards collapsing onto an early DONE. For the last round I keep the baseline's footprint prior and add the legality mask as a learned per-type input to the head. I then try three ways around the exploration problem: a long horizon with a sharp policy, many small updates over several epochs, and a uniform initial policy with high entropy.
